strategy.summary: createBookings() checks room, owner, start alignment (UTC half hour) and length (30–240 min, steps of 30), refuses overlapping bookings of the same room, lists a room's bookings by start time, and lets only the owner cancel. Unit tests with vitest against memoryStore() prove each rule and the refusal (BookingError + its message) beside each accepted path, including boundaries and back-to-back bookings, plus simultaneous requests for one slot.
inScope: BookingError type and message for each refusal
Boundaries: 30/240 minutes, start alignment incl. seconds and non-UTC offsets, adjacent bookings
Simultaneous booking requests for the same slot
outOfScope: The app's database-backed BookingStore (not in the repository)
assumptions: Tests use memoryStore(), as the README says tests do; a fresh createBookings() per test keeps them independent.
Messages are asserted exactly: they are written by the module under test and AC1 requires the error to say why.
Q1 (pending): AC2 covers simultaneous requests too; if two simultaneous bookings of the same slot both succeed, the test is kept as expected-to-fail and a defect is recorded.
The existing at() helper in test/bookings.test.ts moves to test/support/time.ts so both specs import it.
openQuestions: Q1: should AC2 hold for two booking requests made at the same moment?

risks.description: Validation boundaries (30/240 minutes, half-hour alignment) off by one
risks.mitigation: Accepted and refused rows on each side of each boundary

risks.description: Overlap check too strict (rejects back-to-back) or too loose (misses containment)
risks.mitigation: Rows for each overlap shape plus adjacent bookings both ways and other rooms

risks.description: Check-then-add race lets simultaneous requests double-book a room
risks.mitigation: TC11 sends two requests at once

risks.mitigation: TC15 checks refusal and that the booking stays listed

acceptanceCriteria.text: A booking needs a room among Atlas, Borealis, Cosmos, a non-empty owner, a start on the hour or half hour UTC and a length of 30–240 minutes in steps of 30; otherwise book() rejects with a BookingError whose message says why.
A booking overlapping another booking of the same room is rejected with a BookingError; bookings of different rooms never clash, and a booking may start exactly when another ends.
list(room) returns that room's bookings ordered by start time.
Only the booking's owner can cancel it (others get a BookingError), and a cancelled booking's time can be booked again.

testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError 'Atlas is already booked from 2026-03-02T10:00:00.000Z.' and list(Atlas) still holds only ada's booking

books a slot that $shape
steps: it.each: starts when another ends (12:00–13:00), ends when another starts (09:00–10:00)

steps: Promise.allSettled two book() calls for Atlas 10:00 60 min (ada, bob)
testCases.expected: Exactly one fulfilled, one rejected with BookingError; list(Atlas) has one booking

testCases.title: lists a room's bookings by start time
steps: book Atlas 14:00, 09:00, 11:30 in that order and Borealis 10:00
testCases.expected: Starts are 09:00, 11:30, 14:00, and no Borealis booking

preconditions: Atlas 10:00–11:00 by ada, Atlas 12:00 by ada
testCases.expected: List shows only the 12:00 booking; bob's booking resolves

testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError 'Only the person who made a booking can cancel it.'; booking still listed

testCases.title: refuses to cancel a booking that does not exist
testCases.expected: Rejects with BookingError 'There is no booking <id>.'; ada's booking still listed

defects.title: Two simultaneous bookings of the same slot both succeed
defects.description: AC2: a booking that overlaps another booking of the same room must be rejected. book() (src/bookings.ts:55-57) reads store.forRoom(room) and then calls store.add() in a later step. Two book() calls made at the same moment for Atlas 10:00–11:00 both pass the overlap check, so both are stored and the room is double-booked. Expected: one fulfilled and one rejected with BookingError.
defects.evidence: it.fails test 'refuses one of two simultaneous bookings of the same slot' fails as expected: Promise.allSettled statuses are ['fulfilled','fulfilled'] instead of ['fulfilled','rejected'].

review.standard: General test automation standards: reuse the repo's tests and layout / one behaviour proved once (duplication)
review.summary: The new spec repeats cases that test/bookings.test.ts already has under the same `describe('book')`: TC1's Atlas row is the same test as 'books a free room', and TC2's 'Zenith' row (line 20) covers the same refusal as 'refuses a room that does not exist', which only checks the error type. So book() is tested in two files that overlap.
review.failureScenario: If the unknown-room message or the first booking's shape changes, both files fail for the same reason, and the next person has to keep two `describe('book')` blocks in sync. Fix: remove the two old tests from test/bookings.test.ts, or move the new cases into that file, so each behaviour is tested in one place.

questions.question: AC2 says an overlapping booking of the same room is rejected. In the code, book() reads the room's bookings and then adds the new one in a separate step, so two requests for the same slot sent at the same moment can both succeed. Should AC2 cover simultaneous requests too, so this counts as a defect?
questions.assumption: Yes. I'll add a test that sends two simultaneous bookings for the same slot and expects exactly one to be rejected. If it fails, it stays marked expected-to-fail and gets reported as a defect.
questions.answer: No preference from the reviewer: decide yourself from the code, record the decision as an assumption and carry on.
